input.command: git ls-files; ls src/api; cat src/api/*user* 2>/dev/null | head -100
cat test/users.test.js src/db.js migrations/*.js; npm test 2>&1 | tail -30
sed -i "s/full_name: fullName/fullname: fullName/; s/r\.full_name/r.fullname/" src/api/users.js && npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "^# (pass|fail)"; git diff

message:
The users test now passes. I only changed `src/api/users.js`.

**Cause:** the API used the column name `full_name`, but migration `001_create_users.js` creates it as `fullname`. So `db.insert` threw `unknown column users.full_name`.

**Fix:** `createUser` now writes `fullname`, and `getUser` reads `r.fullname`. The public `fullName` field in the API response is unchanged.

The migrations are already applied in production, so I left them alone and changed the API to match the existing schema.
